p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The global transition away from fossil fuels toward a renewable energy matrix is frequently framed as a linear techno-economic evolution, yet it represents an incredibly complex geopolitical and structural bottleneck. While the plummeting levelized cost of solar photovoltaic modules and wind turbines fuels optimism, the inherent intermittency of these green assets exposes the deep inadequacy of legacy electrical grids. Baseload power generation, historically anchored by coal and natural gas, cannot simply be swapped for weather-dependent inputs without triggering severe transmission instability or rolling blackouts. Resolving this structural paralysis requires monumental capital expenditures into utility-scale energy storage systems, smart grid distribution networks, and long-range high-voltage direct current lines. Beyond these engineering hurdles lies a fraught geopolitical landscape; the green transition reshapes global trade dependencies, shifting leverage from petroleum-exporting cartels to nations controlling the extraction and refining of critical minerals like lithium, cobalt, and rare earth elements. Consequently, hasty decarbonization without robust grid orchestration risks triggering severe economic contraction, proving that the energy transition is as much a challenge of geopolitical security as it is of ecological survival.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Pollution in the contemporary world has emerged not merely as an environmental concern but as a reflection of flawed development priorities. Rapid industrialization and unplanned urban expansion have increased the discharge of harmful substances into air, water, and soil. Unlike visible disasters, pollution often progresses silently, accumulating over time before its consequences become evident. Air pollution contributes to chronic respiratory illnesses, while polluted water systems disrupt ecosystems and human health alike. Economic growth frequently takes precedence over ecological protection, weakening regulatory enforcement. Although environmental laws exist, they are often undermined by political pressures and corporate interests. Technological innovations offer temporary relief but rarely address the underlying causes of excessive production and consumption. Public participation in pollution control remains limited, as responsibility is largely shifted to authorities. Consequently, pollution persists as a systemic issue requiring structural, behavioral, and institutional transformation.

questions.q: The term “intermittency” in the passage refers to the fact that renewable sources
opts: are too expensive for developing economies
depend on the weather and do not give a constant flow of power
are using up lithium and cobalt
questions.why: The next sentence calls them “weather-dependent inputs”. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Swapping baseload power for renewables without changing the grid results in
opts: severe transmission instability and possible rolling blackouts
an end to oil cartels' leverage
questions.why: Third sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The green transition alters global geopolitics by
opts: empowering nations that control critical-mineral supply chains
forcing every nation onto HVDC lines
questions.why: Leverage shifts to nations refining lithium, cobalt and rare earths. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author's view on the speed of decarbonisation is that

a rushed transition without grid orchestration can cause economic contraction

an unavoidable outcome of industrial growth
a systemic problem rooted in development patterns

questions.q: Choose the word closest in meaning to “ameliorate”:
questions.why: Ameliorate = make better. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct tense: “By next March, they ______ the new hospital wing.”
questions.why: An action finished before a future time: future perfect. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Spot the error: “Unless you do not submit the form, you cannot sit the exam.”
questions.why: 'Unless' already means 'if not'; drop 'do not'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “People expect the minister to resign.”
opts: The minister is expected to resign.
It is expected the minister to resign.
questions.why: The same pattern as GPSC's 2026 items: subject + is expected + to-infinitive. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “The authority ordered him to submit the documents.”
opts: He was ordered to submit the documents.
He is ordered to submit the documents.
He was ordered submitting the documents.
To submit the documents was ordered to him.
questions.why: Past active becomes 'was ordered'; the infinitive 'to submit' stays. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: After Kushavati district was created, how many talukas does Goa have in all?
questions.why: North Goa 6, South Goa 2, Kushavati 4.

questions.q: In 2026 Rajnath Singh approved transfer of technology to Indian manufacturers for:
The UN declared 2 October, Gandhi Jayanti, the International Day of Non-Violence in:
questions.why: UN General Assembly resolution, 2007.

questions.q: In 2026 India overtook which country to become the world's second-largest solar growth market, adding 37 GW?
India won the Women's T20 Asia Cup 2026. How many times has India won the women's Asia Cup?
questions.why: Shafali Verma was Player of the Tournament. Sep 2026.

questions.q: Who won India's first medal at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games?
questions.why: India finished fourth with 39 medals.

questions.q: In October 2026, Tata Motors raised its offer for the acquisition of:
Who became the first CEO of the Indian Super League under its new club-led model in 2026?
questions.why: The ISL is India's top football league. Sep 2026.

questions.q: India played its first-ever men's T20 International against which country in September 2026?
India's first fully commercial Earth-observation constellation, approved by IN-SPACe in 2026, will have how many satellites?
questions.why: Allied Orbits consortium, to be operational by 2029.

questions.q: P provides premises (₹6,00,000); Q and R put in ₹3,00,000 and ₹5,00,000 cash. P gets rent of ₹5,000 a month; Q and R get 10% interest on capital; the rest is shared 3 : 2 : 5. If Q's total earning is ₹70,000, what was the gross profit?
questions.why: Q's interest 30,000, so his share is 40,000 = 2/10 of the remainder: 2,00,000. Add R's interest 50,000, Q's 30,000 and rent 60,000: 3,40,000. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Find the smallest number which leaves remainder 7 when divided by 12, 18, 21 or 30.
Identify the next term: 1, 2, 6, 42, 1806, …
questions.why: Each term is n × (n + 1) of the previous: 1806 × 1807 = 3263442. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: What day of the week was 15 August 1947?
questions.why: Independence Day 1947 fell on a Friday. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: What is the profit per cent on an article? I. 5% discount is given on the list price. II. Without the discount, the profit would be 20%. III. The cost price is ₹5,000. Which statements are necessary?
questions.why: List = 1.2 × cost, sold at 0.95 × list = 1.14 × cost: 14% profit. The cost figure isn't needed. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: Is the average age of a school's students less than 17? I. Class VIII is under 25% of the school. II. Class VIII averages 18 years; the rest average 16.
questions.why: II alone allows any average between 16 and 18. With I, the weight of 18 is under 25%, so the average is below 16.5. GPSC CBRT, Apr 2024.

questions.q: Who is the fastest of Rani, Supriya and Amita (all different)? I. Rani and Supriya take 5 days; Supriya and Amita take 10 days. II. Rani and Amita take 30/7 days.
questions.why: From I, r − a = 1/10, so Rani beats Amita. Since s + a = 1/10, s is below 1/10 while r is above it, so Rani is fastest. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2024.

questions.q: Piky, Quiky and Riky alone finish an assignment in 7, 8 and 11 days. Together they earn 1,105 coins. Find each share.
Karan beats Arjun by 10 m in a 100 m race. In a second race Karan starts 10 m behind the line. What happens?
questions.why: Speeds 100 : 90. While Karan runs 110 m, Arjun runs 99 m. GPSC CBRT, Jan 2024.

questions.q: In an x m race, Chaupat beats Popat by 18 m and Sarpat by 24 m; Popat beats Sarpat by 8 m. Find x.
questions.why: (x − 24)/(x − 18) = (x − 8)/x gives 2x = 144, so x = 72. GPSC CBRT, Nov 2023.

questions.q: In the sixth edition of the Organon Hahnemann preferred the term:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Earlier editions said 'vital force' (Lebenskraft).

questions.q: Hahnemann (§246, sixth edition) allows repetition of the remedy at suitable intervals provided that:
opts: each dose is given unchanged in the same potency
only placebo is given in between
each dose is slightly modified in potency (by succussion) so the vital force does not resist it
the remedy is changed each time
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. The same unchanged dose repeated would provoke reaction.

questions.q: Hahnemann's 'Lesser Writings' were collected and translated into English by:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Dudgeon also translated the Organon (fifth edition).

questions.q: An organ remedy used in mother tincture for left-sided splenic enlargement and pain is:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Ceanothus is the classic spleen remedy.

questions.q: Eruptions with thick, hard crusts under which yellow pus collects, intense itching, and neuralgia after herpes zoster suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Mezereum: crusts with pus beneath, post-herpetic neuralgia.

questions.q: Profuse sweat on the head of a fat, flabby child is Calcarea carb. A child who is thin, emaciated about the neck, with a craving for salt and a map-like tongue, needs:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Nat mur: emaciation descending from the neck, mapped tongue.

questions.q: The constitutional remedy of the hydrogenoid constitution (worse from damp) is:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Grauvogl's hydrogenoid constitution.

questions.q: A 6C potency represents a dilution of the original substance of:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Each C step is 1:100, so six steps give 10^-12.

questions.q: In the Korsakovian method of potentisation:
opts: the same vial is used throughout, emptied and refilled with fresh vehicle at each step
a new vial is used for each potency
potencies are made only by trituration
the dilution is 1 in 50,000 at each step
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Korsakov's single-vial method; Hahnemannian uses a fresh vial for each step.

questions.q: Gentry's 'Concordance Repertory' is arranged on the pattern of:
opts: a Bible concordance, by key words
questions.why: Six volumes, indexed by significant words.

questions.q: Barthel and Klunker's 'Synthetic Repertory' covers mainly:
opts: Mind, Generalities, and Sleep, Dreams and Sexuality
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Three volumes of general symptoms.

questions.q: Antidiuretic hormone acts mainly on the:
questions.why: It inserts aquaporins and concentrates urine.

questions.q: Cortisol is secreted by the adrenal cortex zone called:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Glomerulosa = aldosterone; reticularis = androgens.

questions.q: Dry gangrene usually results from:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Wet gangrene involves venous congestion and infection.

questions.q: The erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) is typically very high in:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. ESR rises with raised globulins and fibrinogen; it falls in polycythaemia and sickle cell disease.

questions.q: COPD is confirmed on spirometry by a post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC ratio of less than:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. GOLD criterion; the obstruction is not fully reversible.

questions.q: Renal colic, worse on the left, with pains radiating in all directions and bubbling sensations in the kidney, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Berberis: radiating pains, bubbling sensation.

questions.q: Asthma that is worse in damp weather and at 4–5 a.m., with loose rattling and morning diarrhoea, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Natrum sulph: hydrogenoid constitution.

questions.q: Most children's first milk tooth erupts at about:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Lower central incisors.

questions.q: The two most important danger signs in a child with cough or difficult breathing are fast breathing and:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. IMNCI pneumonia signs.

questions.q: Pain and tenderness in the right iliac fossa at McBurney's point suggest:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. One-third of the way from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus.

questions.q: A painful hard swelling of the knee in an elderly person, worse after use, with crepitus, most likely indicates:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Degenerative joint disease.

questions.q: Under Indian criminal law, consent for a medical procedure given by a child under 12 years is:
opts: not valid; consent of the parent or guardian is required
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. A child under 12 cannot give valid consent for acts done for his or her benefit.

questions.q: A 'sentinel surveillance' system is used mainly to:
opts: detect trends in diseases through selected reporting sites
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Used for HIV and others.

questions.q: The 'iceberg phenomenon' of disease refers to:
opts: most cases of a disease being hidden (subclinical or undiagnosed) below the visible clinical cases
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Screening reveals the hidden part.
